Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our latest DPA (redwood_dpa_v3.pdf), a dataflow SVG exported as PNG (redwood_dataflow_viz.png), and a current subprocessor matrix (subprocessor_matrix.csv). See quick answers below; Neha (privacy) is cc'd for technical confirmation.

Quick answers:
- Dataflow: Ingestion occurs in the customer region (EU region by default for AlphaMed). PII can appear in prompts/inputs. We encrypt all data at rest with KMS-managed keys and isolate per-tenant storage buckets. Caching: prefix/KV caches are optional per-customer and can be disabled; when enabled, caches are encrypted and TTL-limited.
- Subprocessors: Listed in the attached CSV. We tier subprocessors by function (compute, storage, monitoring). All EU-crossing subprocessors have SCCs or equivalent provisions; for US-based infra we use SCC + additional contract clauses.
- Access controls: Access to unredacted customer data is restricted to a very small SRE/infra ops group via break-glass workflows; access is logged, time-limited, and audited monthly. Model artifact access is developer-role gated and requires MFA and device attestation.

Could you confirm which elements of the dataflow you'd like expanded (e.g., retention points, anonymization tooling, logging TTLs)? We can produce an annotated diagram showing retention durations and encryption boundaries.

Next steps: 1) Jordan to confirm any redlines to DPA; 2) Neha to provide technical attestations; 3) I can send a DocuSign link once we align.

Thanks,

Jordan — hi, Neha from Privacy here. Adding some specifics you asked for below. Happy to jump on a quick call if you'd like to walk the diagram together.

Technical clarifications:
- Caches: By default we do not persist raw inputs to any global caches. For customers that enable prefix/KV caching, keys are namespaced per-customer and values are encrypted with the customer's KMS key if provided; otherwise encrypted with our account key. TTL is configurable; recommended default is 15m for low-latency workloads.
- Retention: Raw request logs are retained for 30 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring; customers can opt into shorter periods or request deletion. Aggregated telemetry (no PII) is kept for 24 months.
- Access & Break-glass: Break-glass requires two approvers (security + product ops), an entry in the audit log, and automatic email notification to the customer's security contact if the customer has enabled that feature.
- Transfers: For EU->non-EU transfers we rely on SCCs when needed and maintain a list of subprocessors with their locations. For any processor that does on-prem or enclave compute we can provide SCIF-level attestations under NDA.

Also: We can generate an annotated dataflow that explicitly maps PII fields (names, contact, medical IDs) to where they might appear in logs and model context. Let me know if you want field-level mapping or a higher-level diagram.

-Neha
Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
